system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall assessment:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." Its structure is: (a) a low cap, deductible basket and short claims period; (b) extend those limits to *everything* – title, tax, IP, indemnities; (c) then neutralise what is left through blanket data-room disclosure plus a constructive-knowledge defence. Separately, roughly **AUD 4.1m+ of known, quantifiable items** (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 420k plus on-costs, Ironquay 180k, Sandbar 330k) are being pushed into the post-Completion warranty regime rather than dealt with in price or at Completion – against a cap of 4.8m. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the Update on several points (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses), which we should use.

---

## A. Liability architecture (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 20.5)

**1. Fundamental/title warranties subject to general caps and 18 months – reject.**
"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity warranties should be capped at 100% of the purchase price and survive for at least 6 years (NSW limitation period) or 7 years. If we buy shares the Seller doesn't own or that are encumbered, a 20% cap is absurd.

**2. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – reverse the default.**
Limitations should apply *only* to general Warranty Claims. Expressly carve out: fundamental warranties, tax warranties/tax indemnity, specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark, bonuses), leakage/debt-free-cash-free adjustments, covenant breaches (interim period, restraint), and fraud/wilful concealment.

**3. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) applying to "all Claims of any nature" – carve out.**
Must exclude fraud, specific indemnities, completion adjustments and equitable/injunctive relief for covenants. Note also: a non-reliance clause cannot exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 ACL, and NSW courts treat such clauses as evidentiary only. Resist any wording attempting to go further.

**4. Cap 20% / AUD 4.8m – negotiate up.**
Push for 40–50% given the open issues; fall back to 30% plus specific indemnities sitting outside the cap. If the Seller wants a low cap, pair it with (i) a retention/escrow (10–15% for 24 months) and (ii) an express set-off right against deferred amounts.

**5. Thresholds – change the basket to a tipping basket.**
AUD 250k "excess only" is a deductible. Push for first-dollar recovery once the basket is reached; de minimis AUD 10–15k with aggregation of related claims arising from the same facts. Thresholds should not apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.

**6. Time limits.**
18 months general → 24 months (at least one full audit cycle and one FBT/income tax cycle post-Completion). Tax → 7 years / expiry of Commissioner's amendment period plus 60 days. IP and privacy/data warranties → 3 years minimum. The Seller's claim that tax and IP are "settled under the general regime" is simply an assertion; we never agreed it.

---

## B. Disclosure and knowledge – the provisions that gut the warranties

**7. General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2) – reject.**
Require that only matters "fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect" qualify the warranties. Limit public-register disclosure to specified ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches dated and attached. Disclosure must not qualify fundamental warranties or specific indemnities. Data-room cut-off (22 Sept 2026, 5pm) should be locked with an agreed USB/index, and no further "disclosure" by email updates before signing without our consent.

**8. Clause 8.3 Buyer knowledge including matters "discoverable" – delete.**
Constructive knowledge of anything in the data room or public records, combined with item 7, means essentially no warranty claim could ever succeed. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must be limited to the *actual* knowledge of two or three named Buyer deal-team individuals of a specific matter *and* its being a breach, and derived only from the Disclosure Letter itself.

---

## C. Known issues – move these out of the warranty regime

**9. Bluefen (DL §2) – ~30% of revenue; the Seller admits no consent exists.**
The Update says the consent is "addressed" and will be "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure §2 says no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Our position:
- Hard condition precedent: unconditional written consent **and** evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), with no variation to pricing, term or termination rights.
- Seller to use best endeavours (not "reasonable"); Buyer entitled to participate in Bluefen discussions.
- Consider a price protection: deferred consideration or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volumes within 12 months citing change of control.

**10. Riverlark (DL §3) – AUD 3.2m facility; release "following Completion" is unacceptable.**
The deal is debt-free/cash-free. Change of control (cl 8.1) will trigger default on Completion. Require at Completion: payoff letter, repayment from the purchase price via the funds flow, deed of release, PPSR discharge, release of any share mortgage or guarantees, and delivery of any share certificates/title documents held by the bank. If the Seller insists on post-Completion release, the full 3.2m plus break costs must be deducted from the price with a Seller indemnity outside the cap. Also confirm via PPSR whether Riverlark holds security over the *shares* – which directly affects item 15.

**11. Completion bonuses (DL §5) – AUD 420k not in the funds flow.**
"A matter for the Seller" is meaningless if the Company pays them post-Completion out of our money. These are Transaction Costs: either paid by the Seller pre-Completion (with evidence) or deducted from price including super (12%), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and any PAYG/leave accruals – gross exposure likely ~AUD 500k. Because of the continued-employment condition, amounts crystallising post-Completion should be placed in escrow or covered by a dollar-for-dollar indemnity. Check whether the Seller is counting on bonuses to retain key staff and whether terms are acceptable to us as new employer.

**12. Ironquay IP (DL §4) – Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables.**
Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of Project Materials on payment of *every* SOW3 fee; 180k is open and no assignment exists. If SOW3 materials form part of the product, the IP ownership warranty is untrue today. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers 180k of fees, not the loss of IP or third-party claims. Require: payment and a confirmatory IP assignment (and moral rights consents) as a condition precedent or completion deliverable; a specific indemnity for all loss from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed IP, outside cap/thresholds; and DD confirmation of SOW1/SOW2 status.

**13. DD-006 privacy/export incident (DL §6) – not "preliminary operational."**
~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external recipient is potentially an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (assessment within 30 days; OAIC and individual notification; civil penalties for serious interferences now up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3x benefit or 30% of turnover). There may also be customer-contract notification obligations (likely Bluefen or Mossvale data). Require: completed assessment and privacy-lawyer report pre-signing; evidence of recipient deletion/undertaking; warranty that all required notifications have been made; specific indemnity (outside caps, 6-year survival) for regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation. Seller's "not expected to be material" is not a position we should accept while the investigation remains preliminary.

**14. Sandbar renewals (DL §8) – three x AUD 110k = 330k.**
Three identically sized contracts to be "read together" looks like splitting to stay under a materiality or approval threshold. Need: the documents, dates, whether entered pre- or post-locked-box/Accounts date, whether terminable, and whether accrued. If not reflected in the Accounts/working capital, treat as leakage or price deduction. Interim covenants should prohibit new commitments above an aggregate (not per-contract) threshold.

**15. Title (DL §10 / Update) – a share register is not title verification.**
Obtain and attach: current ASIC company extract, constitution (pre-emptive rights, director consent to transfer), PPSR search for security over shares (see Riverlark), confirmation of no options, convertibles or shareholder agreements, and share certificates. Fundamental warranties on title must be unqualified by disclosure.

**16. Lease and Mossvale (DL §§7, 9) – lower risk but tidy up.**
Lease: make the DD-007 notification a completion deliverable and obtain Seller warranty that no landlord consent is required. Mossvale: confirm there is no change-of-control clause as distinct from the assignment restriction; obtain warranty.

---

## D. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Push-back |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental warranties capped/time-limited | 100% of price; 6–7 years |
| 2 | Limitations apply to all Claims | Apply to general Warranty Claims only; express carve-outs |
| 3 | Exclusive remedy/non-reliance | Carve out fraud, indemnities, adjustments, ACL |
| 4 | 20% cap | 40–50% target; 30% + escrow and set-off fallback |
| 5 | Deductible basket | Tipping basket; lower de minimis; aggregation |
| 6 | 18-month period; tax/IP "settled" | 24 months general; tax 7 yrs; IP/privacy 3 yrs |
| 7 | Blanket data-room/public-record disclosure | "Fairly disclosed" standard; specific searches only |
| 8 | Buyer constructive knowledge (8.3) | Delete |
| 9 | Bluefen | Hard CP incl. 11.3 conditions; Buyer-approved form; price protection |
| 10 | Riverlark | Payoff and release *at* Completion; price deduction otherwise |
| 11 | Bonuses | Transaction Cost deducted with on-costs; escrow for post-Completion amounts |
| 12 | Ironquay | Payment + assignment as CP; uncapped IP-title indemnity |
| 13 | DD-006 | Complete assessment pre-signing; uncapped privacy indemnity |
| 14 | Sandbar | Full review; leakage/price treatment; aggregate interim covenant |
| 15 | Title | Independent verification; PPSR; unqualified title warranties |
| 16 | Lease/Mossvale | Completion deliverable and warranties |

**Deal-level recommendation:** Known items approach the proposed cap before any unknown warranty breach. Insist that Riverlark, bonuses and Ironquay are resolved in the price/funds flow and at Completion, with Bluefen as a true condition precedent and DD-006 covered by a standalone indemnity. Consider a 10–15% retention for 24 months and, if the Seller holds at a low cap, explore W&I insurance (noting the known issues will be excluded and must be covered by Seller indemnities regardless).

*This is a preliminary review of the summarised positions; the full SPA, Schedule 7 and the DD-002 to DD-012 source documents should be checked before mark-up is issued.*
=== END ADVICE ===
